name: Sickle Cell Disease
description: Sickle cell disease is an inherited blood disorder that affects hemoglobin and red blood cells.
genetics: Changes in the HBB gene can produce an altered form of hemoglobin.
analysis: This case demonstrates how a small DNA change can change a codon and the amino acid produced from it.
note: This is an educational example and is not a medical diagnostic test.

name: Cystic Fibrosis
description: Cystic fibrosis is an inherited condition that can affect the lungs and digestive system.
genetics: Changes in the CFTR gene can affect the function of the CFTR protein.
analysis: This case demonstrates how comparing DNA sequences can help identify a genetic difference.
note: Many different CFTR variants exist. This simplified case is only for educational demonstration.

name: Beta-Thalassemia
description: Beta-thalassemia affects the production of beta-globin, an important part of hemoglobin.
genetics: Variants in the HBB gene can affect the production or function of beta-globin.
analysis: The case demonstrates how a DNA sequence difference can be investigated using sequence comparison.
note: This is a simplified educational case and does not represent clinical testing.

name: Phenylketonuria (PKU)
description: PKU is an inherited condition in which the body has difficulty processing the amino acid phenylalanine.
genetics: Changes in the PAH gene can reduce the activity of the enzyme involved in processing phenylalanine.
analysis: This case demonstrates how genetic changes can be connected to changes in biological processes.
note: This is an educational demonstration and is not a diagnostic test.

name: Huntington Disease
description: Huntington disease is an inherited condition that affects the nervous system.
genetics: It is associated with an expanded CAG repeat in the HTT gene.
analysis: This case introduces the idea that genetic conditions can involve changes in repeated DNA sequences.
note: This is a simplified educational representation and is not a clinical repeat-length test.

name: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
description: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is an inherited condition that causes progressive muscle weakness.
genetics: Changes in the DMD gene can affect dystrophin, a protein important for muscle cells.
analysis: This case demonstrates the relationship between genes and protein function.
note: This is a simplified educational example and is not clinical testing.

name: High Blood Pressure
description: High blood pressure can be influenced by genetics, lifestyle, age, and environmental factors.
genetics: There is no single DNA change that can be used by this application to diagnose high blood pressure.
analysis: This case demonstrates that genetics can contribute to a condition while other factors also play important roles.
note: This section is educational. DNA analysis cannot diagnose high blood pressure.

name: Type 2 Diabetes
description: Type 2 diabetes is influenced by genetic, lifestyle, and environmental factors.
genetics: Many genes can contribute to susceptibility, but there is no single DNA sequence that this application can use to diagnose type 2 diabetes.
analysis: This case demonstrates the idea that genetics can influence disease risk together with lifestyle and environmental factors.
note: This section is educational. DNA analysis cannot diagnose type 2 diabetes.
